The behavior-tracking core is a rolling profile in @region:patterns ('your longest blocks are before 11am; Slack is your top interruption') that the agent refines as more sessions accumulate, driving an adaptive suggestion in @region:coach. When a block beats a personal best it ui_highlight/pulses the tile and ui_notify; when interruptions spike it ui_theme to a calmer accent and recommends a specific protected window. Example: after three focused morning blocks and two interruption-riddled afternoon ones, the coach panel recommends 'protect 9-11am, batch Slack to 2pm' and the patterns panel updates its stated best window as later sessions land.

title: Sepsis Timeline Scrubber
interaction: time-scrubber simulation with intervention what-if
requirement: Regions: @scrubber (a time slider / play control over an ICU stay), @vitals (a multi-series line chart of HR, MAP, RR, temp, SpO2, lactate), @scores (stat tiles for SOFA, qSOFA, NEWS2, shock index), and @events (an intervention log). As the clinician scrubs the timeline the page posts the current hour via ui_state; the agent recomputes the severity scores at that timepoint, redraws the vitals up to the cursor, ui_highlight pulses any score tile crossing a red threshold (lactate >4, MAP <65, qSOFA >=2), and switches ui_theme to an alert accent during a deterioration window. A what-if toggle lets the user apply a hypothetical intervention (e.g. a 30 mL/kg fluid bolus at hour 6) and the agent re-simulates the downstream MAP/lactate trajectory and re-scores. Concrete: scrubbing to hour 8 shows MAP 58, lactate 4.2, qSOFA 3, so the score panel flashes and a 'septic shock window' banner appears; applying the bolus flattens the lactate curve on re-render. The loop is scrub or toggle -> recompute scores -> re-render vitals + attention shift.

title: Study ROI Simulator
interaction: slider study-hour allocation what-if that surfaces the highest-return course
requirement: Expose an @region:inputs with an editable course table (current grade, credit weight, remaining assignment weight) and one 'extra hours/week' slider per course (0-15), plus a @region:projection and a @region:advice. Whenever a grade cell is edited or a slider moves, the page writes ui_state and the agent recomputes each course's projected final grade under a diminishing-returns model and the resulting overall GPA, re-rendering @region:projection with a before/after GPA stat and a bar chart of marginal GPA-points-per-hour by course. It ui_highlight's the single highest-ROI course (steepest marginal return) and writes a plain-language recommendation into @region:advice ('2 more hours in Chemistry beats 6 in History'). Concrete drive: with Chemistry at 71% carrying a heavy final and History at 89%, sliding the weekly budget to 6 hours makes the agent concentrate 5 hours on Chemistry, project GPA 3.1->3.4, and highlight Chemistry's bar. Everything is what-if — no plan is committed, the agent just re-simulates on each change.

title: Deliberation Drift Room
interaction: multi-round Socratic ui_ask that tracks opinion drift and adapts its attacks
requirement: The HTML shows a `@dilemma` region (a select of preset moral/policy dilemmas plus a custom textarea), a `@dialog` region, and a `@drift` region. After the user picks a dilemma the agent uses ui_ask each round to collect their position on a 1-7 scale plus a one-line justification, then plays a targeted devil's advocate that steelmans the strongest counter to the user's specific reasoning rather than generic objections. It records each round's (position, confidence, justification) in ui_state and renders a ui_chart line of opinion drift over rounds plus a ui_stat of 'confidence volatility' into `@drift`, using ui_highlight to mark the round where the stance moved most and to focus the justification that proved fragile. The agent tracks which argument types actually move this user (data vs. values vs. analogy) and concentrates future challenges there. After about five rounds it ui_panels a reflection card summarizing whether the user updated on evidence or dug in. Example: on 'should cities ban cars downtown?', a user starting at 6 who slides to 3 after an equity argument gets that round highlighted and future prompts leaning on equity framings. The loop: state position -> agent challenges the weak point -> re-poll -> drift chart and adaptation.

title: Crawl Forge
interaction: drag monsters/traps into rooms with live difficulty balancing
requirement: Build a tabletop dungeon-encounter designer and difficulty balancer. The page shows a `@dungeon` region of three room slots and a `@palette` region of draggable elements (goblin CR 1/4, ogre CR 2, spike trap, treasure chest, boss), plus a party setup input (e.g. '4 players, level 3'). As the user drags elements into rooms, the agent computes each room's encounter difficulty budget against the party, estimates TPK probability and expected rounds via a monte-carlo-ish model, and totals loot value, rendering a balance dashboard: per-room stat tiles, a ui_chart bar of challenge-vs-target per room, and a pacing table. It uses ui_highlight to outline rooms that are wildly over- or under-tuned (red for deadly, gray for trivial) and ui_notify to summarize 'Room 2 is a likely TPK.' A 'balance it' button makes the agent auto-adjust monster counts and re-render as an explicit before/after what-if of the difficulty numbers. A tester can stack three ogres into one room, see it flash deadly with an 82% TPK stat, click balance, and watch it recompose into a survivable fight.

title: Fairness Audit Console
interaction: ui_ask-configured audit loop that drills groups and applies remedies
requirement: The page exposes @region:setup, @region:disparity, @region:groups, and @region:remedy. The agent begins with ui_ask in @region:setup to learn which protected attributes and fairness criterion matter (e.g., 'audit by [sex][age band][region]; target: [equal opportunity][demographic parity]'), BLOCKING on the form. It then composes a disparity dashboard: a ui_panel into @region:disparity with grouped-bar ui_chart of selected-rate / TPR / FPR per group and stat tiles for the largest gap, plus a per-group ui_table in @region:groups. It ui_highlight's the group with the worst disparity and ui_theme shifts to a caution accent if any gap breaches the 80%-rule. When the user clicks a flagged group the agent drills into its confusion breakdown and uses ui_ask to offer remedies (reweight / per-group threshold / drop proxy feature) rendered into @region:remedy, then re-runs and re-renders the deltas. Concrete: choose sex + equal-opportunity → TPR 0.88 (male) vs 0.74 (female), gap flagged; apply per-group thresholds and the agent shows the gap shrinking to 0.03 with a ui_notify confirmation.

title: Layout Critique Coach
interaction: a guided attention walk that spotlights one design issue at a time
requirement: Provide @region:canvas holding an agent-built representative layout, @region:notes for a ranked critique list, and @region:focus for a single-issue spotlight, with a template select (landing / poster / email), a 'next issue' button, and a severity filter. The user picks a template or describes their own layout; the agent renders a representative mock into @region:canvas, runs a hierarchy/contrast/spacing critique, and produces a severity-ranked issue list in @region:notes. Then it enters a guided walk: each 'next issue' click makes the agent ui_highlight (focus + pulse) the offending element, use ui_layout to show a before/after split in @region:focus, and explain the specific fix — attention-direction is the core interaction, not a side effect. Drive it with a SaaS landing hero that has four competing CTAs: issue one spotlights the CTA cluster and dims the rest, issue two moves the focus to a 2.8:1 subhead contrast failure. The walk continues issue by issue until the list is exhausted, and the severity filter re-orders which issues the walk visits.

title: Post-Mortem Timeline Forge
interaction: structured retro conducted entirely through ui_ask
requirement: Author regions: @timeline (a horizontal event ribbon), @factors (contributing versus mitigating tags), and @actions (a follow-ups table). Starting from a one-line incident title, the agent conducts a structured retro entirely through ui_ask, one question per turn — 'What was the first signal, and at what time?', 'When did a human first acknowledge?', 'What made it worse?', 'What stopped the bleeding?' — placing each answer as a dated node on @timeline and tagging it into @factors. It computes and ui_stat's the derived intervals (time-to-detect, time-to-mitigate, time-to-resolve), and once the ribbon is populated it ui_highlight's the largest gap (usually detection) as the key improvement area. It then ui_render's an action-items table with owners into @actions and, via a final ui_ask, lets the user accept or edit each item. The finished dashboard is a full incident report the user assembled by answering questions rather than typing prose, with the agent composing the artifact from the accumulated answers turn by turn.

title: Tilt Journal Coach
interaction: log-driven behavior tracking that reshapes coaching
requirement: Render an @entry region with a log-a-trade form (ticker, direction, size, an entry-emotion select of calm / FOMO / revenge / bored, and P/L), a @history table region, and an @insights coach region. Each submit appends to a ui_state journal, after which the agent recomputes behavioral metrics — win rate by emotion, average size when 'revenge' versus 'calm,' overtrading days, time-of-day clustering — and re-renders the recent-trades table, a ui_chart bar of P/L by emotion, and a coach panel whose advice adapts to the accumulated pattern (e.g., 'your revenge trades are 3x larger and lose 70% — capping size when tilted would have saved $2,100'). It ui_highlights the emotion row costing the most, cools the ui_theme toward a calm palette when it detects a tilt streak, and fires ui_notify after three trades in one day. The loop is pure behavior tracking: each new logged trade re-shapes the metrics and the coaching. Concrete test: a fifth trade tagged 'revenge' at -$400 should trigger a two-loss-tilt-streak flag, pulse the revenge row, and toast 'step away — your last 3 tilt trades all lost.'

title: PID Tuning Dojo
interaction: slider tuning plus an auto-tune ui_ask that adapts to the user's habits
requirement: Author regions: @plant (a selector for thermal oven / DC motor / quadrotor altitude), @gains (Kp, Ki, Kd sliders), @response (a step-response chart), and @metrics (overshoot and settling stats). The user picks the DC motor and sets Kp = 4, Ki = 1.2, Kd = 0.1, pushing state through ui_state. The agent simulates the closed-loop step response, uses ui_chart to draw it into @response, ui_panel to mount overshoot percent, settling time, and steady-state error into @metrics, and ui_highlight to mark the overshoot peak. The agent uses ui_state to track the full sequence of gain edits and the user's apparent target, and after a few attempts uses ui_ask to offer 'want me to auto-tune toward under 5% overshoot?' then proposes gains and re-simulates. It adapts its coaching to the user's pattern — for instance, if they repeatedly over-crank Kp, it warns about that tendency before they do it again.

title: Weekly Review Cartographer
interaction: click-to-triage status chips with a closing commitment ask
requirement: Expose @region:progress (a review-steps checklist), @region:inbox, @region:projects, @region:map, and @region:commit. The user pastes a brain-dump of tasks and projects, and the agent renders them as inbox cards each carrying clickable status chips (Active / Someday / Waiting / Done). Each chip click posts ui_state; the agent sorts the item into a ui_panel Projects board (Active / Someday / Waiting columns), shrinks the ui_render inbox, advances the @region:progress checklist, and grows a ui_graph in @region:map linking projects to their next actions. It tracks which projects have repeatedly been deferred or have no next action across the dump and ui_highlight those as stalled, and for any item the user marks Active without a next action it ui_ask 'what's the very next action?'. When the inbox hits zero it renders the week's three committed next-actions into @region:commit and ui_notify 'inbox to zero.' Example: a 12-item dump triages into 5 active / 4 someday / 3 waiting, two projects with no next action get flagged stalled, and the commit panel surfaces the top three.

title: Evidence Triage Screener
interaction: swipe-decision active-learning loop
requirement: A @current region shows one study's title + abstract with Include / Exclude / Maybe buttons and a reason input; a @queue region lists the remaining abstracts ranked by predicted relevance; a @progress region tracks screened count, include rate, and estimated recall. The user states the review question and PICO (e.g. 'RCTs of SGLT2 inhibitors on HF hospitalization in T2D adults'); each decision is captured in ui_state, and the agent updates a lightweight relevance model from the accumulating include/exclude features (keywords, study type, population), then re-ranks the @queue so likely-includes float to the top and ui_highlight marks the ones matching the learned pattern. It periodically surfaces a rationale card ('you exclude non-RCTs and pediatric studies, so I deprioritized 42 of them') and flags borderline abstracts for a second look. Concrete: after the user excludes three observational cohort abstracts, the agent demotes all observational studies and promotes double-blind RCTs to the top of the queue. The loop is decide -> learn from the accumulated pattern -> re-rank -> present the next abstract.

title: Reading Ladder Calibrator
interaction: adaptive reading-level ui_ask loop that tunes passage complexity to comprehension
requirement: Expose a @region:passage, a @region:quiz, and a sidebar @region:meter with a reading-level gauge. The agent presents a short passage at an estimated level (e.g. Lexile ~800), then uses ui_ask to pose two or three comprehension questions spanning main-idea, vocabulary-in-context, and inference, scoring each. It tracks per-question-type accuracy across the session in ui_state and adjusts the next passage's complexity up if the reader aces inference, or down with a brief vocabulary pre-teach if they miss literal questions. After each round it ui_render's @region:meter with the current estimated level, a trend line, and a per-skill breakdown, and ui_highlight's the weakest comprehension skill. Concrete drive: the reader nails main-idea but misses two inference questions across two rounds; the agent holds the level, injects an inference-strategy tip, and selects an inference-rich next passage rather than climbing. The loop runs a fixed number of rounds or until the level stabilizes, ending with a summary panel.

title: Bias Audit Journal
interaction: adaptive ui_ask interview building a live bias profile
requirement: The page exposes a `@decision` region (textarea to describe a decision you're weighing plus inputs for the competing options), an `@interview` region, and a `@profile` region. The agent runs a structured ui_ask interview - one probing question at a time (e.g., 'What evidence would change your mind?', 'What did the option you rejected have going for it?') - and after each answer scores signals of specific biases (confirmation, sunk-cost, anchoring, availability, overconfidence) into ui_state. It renders a live ui_chart (radar of bias exposure) plus a ui_table (bias, trigger quote, debiasing prompt) into `@profile`, and crucially chooses the next question adaptively to probe whichever biases currently score highest, using ui_highlight to spotlight the dominant one. When a bias crosses a threshold the agent ui_notifies a concrete debiasing move (pre-mortem, reference-class forecast, steelman the alternative) and re-asks the core decision to see whether the user's confidence recalibrates. Example: 'I should keep funding this project because we've already spent $2M' should spike sunk-cost, spotlight it, and trigger a pre-mortem prompt. The loop: answer -> bias radar updates -> agent targets the next question at your weak spot -> debias -> recheck.

title: Metropolis Zoner
interaction: paint zoning tiles on a grid with a live city simulation
requirement: Build a city-builder zoning sandbox on an interactive grid. The `@city-grid` region is an 8x8 clickable tile map; a `@brush` region lets the user pick a zone type (residential, commercial, industrial, park, road) and paint tiles. After each paint stroke the agent simulates the city — traffic flow along roads, pollution spread from industry, land value, tax revenue, and citizen happiness — and renders a dashboard into `@stats`: stat tiles (population, happiness %, monthly budget), a ui_chart line of happiness over simulated years, and a demand table (is the city short on jobs or homes?). It uses ui_highlight to flag gridlocked intersections and pollution hotspots on the grid, and shifts ui_theme from a warm palette toward a toxic tint as citywide pollution climbs, with ui_notify calling out milestones ('unemployment over 20%'). Because the simulation reruns on every stroke, a tester can wall a residential block behind heavy industry and watch happiness and land value slump while the poisoned tiles light up, then drop in parks and see the trend line recover.

title: Feature Pipeline Composer
interaction: drag-to-compose transform pipeline with live distribution simulation
requirement: The page exposes @region:blocks (draggable transform blocks: log-scale, standardize, one-hot, target-encode, winsorize, PCA, SMOTE), a sequential @region:pipeline drop lane, @region:effect, and @region:health. The user drags transform blocks into the pipeline lane in order and each drop or reorder posts the ordered pipeline via ui_state. The agent simulates the pipeline on a sample profile and re-renders the effect: a ui_panel into @region:effect with before/after distribution ui_chart(bar histogram) for a chosen column and stat tiles (skew, cardinality, feature count, leakage risk), updating on every edit. It validates ordering and uses ui_highlight and ui_notify to warn on foot-guns (SMOTE before the train/test split, standardize before one-hot, target-encode risking leakage), ui_render-ing a pipeline-health verdict into @region:health. Concrete: drag winsorize then standardize onto 'monthly_charges' and the agent shows skew dropping 1.8 → 0.2; insert target-encode on 'zip' and it flags leakage and suggests K-fold encoding, keeping the composed pipeline and its simulated effect in lockstep as the user rearranges blocks.

title: Logline Doctor
interaction: a ui_ask refinement loop that scores five story dimensions on a radar
requirement: Lay out @region:logline for the evolving one-sentence pitch, @region:radar for a five-axis radar (protagonist clarity, want, obstacle, stakes, ironic hook), and @region:log for a revision-history table, with a genre select and a 'tighten' button. The agent drives via ui_ask, asking one targeted question at a time — who is the protagonist, what do they want, what stands in the way, what is at stake, what is the ironic twist — and after each blocking answer it rewrites the logline, re-renders the radar as that dimension firms up, and appends the new version to the history table. Seed it with just 'a chef': across five asks the logline grows into 'a burned-out three-star chef must cook for the food critic who ended her career — without knowing it's him.' When all five axes are scored the user hits 'tighten' and the agent proposes a punchier cut and re-scores, and any weak axis can be revisited by re-opening its ui_ask. The dashboard and the ask loop stay in lockstep every turn.

title: Warehouse Throughput Lab
interaction: slider what-if that surfaces the moving bottleneck
requirement: Author region @levers holds sliders for pickers on shift (5-60), dock doors open (2-12), inbound order volume (1k-10k/day), and automation coverage (0-100%), plus a 'peak season' preset; @panels holds the model output. The agent treats the facility as a staged queueing system (receive -> pick -> pack -> ship) and on every lever change recomputes throughput (orders/hour), utilization per stage, backlog growth, and labor cost, re-rendering a ui_chart of stage utilization and a ui_stat row (throughput, backlog, cost/order) into @panels. Crucially it identifies the current bottleneck stage by theory-of-constraints and ui_highlight's it, with a one-line note on the cheapest lever to relieve it. For example, 20 pickers, 6 doors, and 5000 orders/day should peg dock doors as the constraint and suggest opening two more before adding pickers. Hitting the peak-season preset bumps volume so the operator can stress-test staffing, and the agent re-narrates how the bottleneck moves, keeping the what-if loop tightly coupled to attention.

title: Rate Setter War Room
interaction: multi-turn central-banker simulation with compounding consequences
requirement: The user plays central banker: expose a @dial region with a policy-rate slider and a 'Set rate for this quarter' submit button, an @economy dashboard region, and a @timeline history region. Each quarter, given the chosen rate, the agent advances a small macro simulation (Phillips-curve / Taylor-rule dynamics with lags) updating inflation, unemployment, GDP growth, and a market-confidence reading, then re-renders a dashboard (inflation-vs-target line, unemployment line, GDP bar, confidence gauge) and appends the decision and its outcome to a running timeline chart. It injects news shocks via ui_notify (oil spike, banking stress) that the user must respond to next quarter, ui_highlights any indicator breaching a mandate threshold, and reddens the ui_theme if a recession or runaway inflation triggers. The loop runs multi-turn: the user sets a rate each quarter, the agent simulates and re-renders, and consequences compound across roughly eight quarters toward a scored soft-landing / stagflation / recession outcome held in ui_state. Concrete test: with inflation at 6%, hiking to 5.5% eases next-quarter inflation to ~4.8% but lifts unemployment to ~5.2%, the timeline logs it, and a toast reads 'soft-landing narrative holding.'

title: Spectral ID Detective
interaction: ui_ask interrogation of a spectrum that tracks which clues the user misreads
requirement: Regions are @spectrum (an IR or mass-spec plot), @clue-log (accumulated deductions), and @guess (the final-structure submission form). The agent presents an unknown compound's IR spectrum via ui_chart into @spectrum — e.g. a strong ~1715 cm-1 C=O band, a broad 2500-3300 cm-1 O-H, and a molecular ion at m/z = 60 — then uses ui_ask to ask which functional group each flagged band implies. On each answer it reacts, uses ui_render to write confirmed and eliminated groups into @clue-log, and ui_highlight to point at the next diagnostic band. It uses ui_state to track which clues the user misreads (for example repeatedly confusing a ketone C=O with an acid C=O) and adapts the difficulty and the phrasing of subsequent hints to that pattern, narrowing the candidate set until the user submits a final structure (acetic acid) and the agent scores the deduction path.

title: Zettel Weaver
interaction: click-a-node to expand and accept suggested links
requirement: Expose @region:paste (notes in), @region:graph, @region:node (focused-note detail), and @region:gaps. The user pastes several atomic notes; the agent extracts concepts and builds a ui_graph of note and concept nodes (edges = shared concept or explicit link) into @region:graph, with ui_stat tiles (notes, links, orphans) in @region:gaps. Clicking any node makes the agent ui_render that note's detail plus its neighbors and a 'suggested links to notes X, Y (because…)' block in @region:node, and ui_highlight the suggested target nodes in the graph; accepting a suggestion adds the edge and recomputes the orphan count. The agent continuously ui_highlight orphan notes with no links and proposes a bridging concept to connect the two largest disconnected clusters, ui_notify once the graph becomes fully connected. Example: pasting six notes on attention, memory, and spaced repetition yields a graph with one orphan note on 'sleep'; clicking it, the agent suggests linking it to 'memory consolidation,' and accepting drops the orphan count to zero.

title: Polypharmacy Deprescribing Board
interaction: interaction-graph plus ui_ask accept/reject loop
requirement: The user assembles a medication list in a @meds region (add drug + dose chips); the agent builds an @interactions region as a ui_graph where nodes are drugs and edges are flagged interactions (severity-colored), a @burden region of stat tiles (anticholinergic burden score, sedative load, renal-risk count, total pill count), and a @plan region. Each turn the agent proposes one deprescribing or substitution step via ui_ask ('Taper amitriptyline: high anticholinergic burden in an 82-year-old; accept / modify / decline?'), and on the user's answer it recomputes the interaction graph and burden tiles, with ui_highlight fading the removed node and its edges. It tracks in ui_state which drug classes the user tends to accept or refuse and orders later suggestions to fit that pattern, stopping once burden falls below target and rendering a final reconciled list in @plan. Concrete: a list with amitriptyline + oxybutynin + diphenhydramine shows an anticholinergic burden of 9 and a dense interaction cluster; accepting two swaps drops the score to 3 and dissolves the cluster. The loop is propose -> user decides -> recompute graph/burden -> next tailored proposal.

title: Recall Heatmap Drill
interaction: click-to-drill mastery heatmap that adapts to accumulated recall behavior
requirement: Expose a @region:heatmap rendering the deck as a grid of cells colored by mastery from ui_state per-card history (red=lapsed, amber=learning, green=strong), a central @region:drill, and a @region:stats. The user clicks any cell or a 'drill weakest cluster' button; the agent pulls that card or cluster into @region:drill, shows the prompt, and on reveal ui_ask's a self-graded 'got it / missed it' that updates the card's ease and interval and recolors its heatmap cell live. It tracks streaks, review timing, and which semantic tags cluster as weak (e.g. 'irregular preterite verbs'), surfacing that pattern in @region:stats as a bar chart and ui_highlight'ing the weakest tag-cluster on the heatmap. Concrete drive: the user clicks a red cluster of Spanish irregular verbs, misses 'supe', the cell stays red, and the stats panel promotes 'irregular preterite' to the top weak tag with a recommended focused session. The user drives entirely by clicking cells while the dashboard reshapes itself around their accumulated performance.

title: Whip-Count War Room
interaction: drag legislators across vote columns with amendment what-if simulation
requirement: The HTML lays out a `@roster` region as three columns (Yes / Undecided / No) seeded with about 15 legislator cards, each showing party, district lean, and a top issue, plus a `@tally` region and a `@levers` region. Dragging a card between columns updates ui_state; the agent recomputes the whip count against the passage threshold, renders a ui_chart (votes vs. needed) and a ui_stat ('+2 to pass') into `@tally`, and uses ui_highlight to spotlight the pivotal swing members whose flip changes the outcome. In `@levers` the agent proposes concrete amendments and trades (each a button) and, on click or hover, simulates which undecideds would move and at what cost to your existing Yes bloc, previewing the new tally before commit. It uses ui_ask when two strategies conflict ('Amendment A wins Rep. Diaz but loses your progressive flank - proceed?') and branches on the answer. Example: a bill at 48/50 with 4 undecided should highlight the two cheapest-to-flip members and propose a rural-carveout amendment that moves them. The loop: drag to whip -> live tally and pivotal highlight -> agent simulates amendment levers -> commit or ask.

title: Risk Cartel
interaction: click-to-attack a territory map against an AI that learns your style
requirement: Build a territory-conquest game where the agent is an adaptive opponent. The `@war-map` region shows ~10 connected regions across three continents with troop counts and ownership colors; the user clicks an owned region then an adjacent enemy region to attack, or clicks to place reinforcements. The agent resolves combat with dice-odds probability, updates troop counts and ownership, uses ui_notify for the battle result and ui_highlight to trace the shifting front line. It composes a war-room dashboard in `@warroom`: continent-control bars (ui_chart), troop-total stat tiles, and a threat table. Crucially, it records the player's strategy in ui_state — do they turtle or blitz, which continent they favor, whether they over-commit — and adapts its own AI moves to counter, reinforcing the front the player keeps hitting and opening a second front where the player is thin. A tester can spend three turns hammering one border and watch the AI stop defending elsewhere, fortify exactly that border, and open a flanking push into the continent the player abandoned, with the war-room table calling out the new pressure.

title: Serving Cost & Latency Simulator
interaction: slider what-if over deployment knobs that redraws the cost/latency frontier
requirement: The page exposes @region:knobs (sliders and selects for replicas, batch size, quantization int8/fp16/fp32, GPU type, and target QPS), @region:frontier, and @region:budget, seeded with a base model profile (a 7B LLM at ~40ms/token fp16 on an A10). The agent renders a serving dashboard: a ui_panel into @region:frontier with a latency-vs-throughput ui_chart(line) and stat tiles (p99 latency, max QPS, $/1k requests, monthly cost, GPU utilization). As the user turns any knob the page posts the config; the agent recomputes a queueing/throughput model (int8 ~1.7x throughput and lower cost with a small quality caveat; more replicas cut queue latency but raise cost) and re-renders the frontier plus cost tiles, using ui_highlight to flash p99 when it breaches an SLA line. When monthly cost exceeds a stated budget the agent ui_notify's and ui_render's the cheapest SLA-meeting config into @region:budget. Concrete: 2 replicas fp16 batch 8 → p99 320ms, $2.4k/mo; switch to int8 + batch 16 → p99 210ms, $1.5k/mo and the agent flags the quality caveat as the frontier redraws.

title: Type Pairing Studio
interaction: select and slide vibe controls to re-rank live type-pairing recommendations
requirement: Expose @region:controls with a heading-vibe select (geometric / humanist / serif-display), a body-vibe select, and contrast, formality, and era sliders; @region:specimens with live specimen cards showing H1, body, and caption in each candidate pairing; and @region:score with a scorecard. On any control change the agent recommends three font pairings matching the settings, renders real-text specimen panels into @region:specimens, scores each on contrast, harmony, and legibility into a table plus a ui_chart bar in @region:score, and ui_highlights the recommended pick. The what-if: start at humanist heading / low contrast, then drag the contrast slider high — the agent re-ranks the pairings, swaps the specimen panels, moves the highlight to the new winner, and posts ui_notify 'now favoring a serif-display + grotesque pairing for stronger hierarchy.' All control values persist in ui_state so each adjustment re-enters the same recommendation simulation rather than starting over.

title: Disaster Resource Allocator
interaction: drag scarce assets onto zones with ui_ask command decisions
requirement: Author regions: @zones (a grid of affected areas, each a card with casualty count, access status, and current coverage), @assets (draggable pools of ambulances, medical crews, and shelter beds), and @status (an unmet-need and response-time summary). Seed with 4 zones — e.g. Zone C: 60 casualties, road access severed — and deliberately scarce assets. The user drags assets onto zones; each allocation makes the agent recompute coverage ratio, projected response time, and total unmet need, rendering ui_stat totals and a ui_chart of unmet-need-by-zone into @status and ui_highlight'ing any zone still critically under-resourced. When a hard trade-off appears the agent uses ui_ask to force a command decision ('Zone C road out and 60 casualties — reroute ground units 40 min or request air evac?'), and it periodically injects a fresh casualty report via ui_notify that shifts priorities and forces reallocation. The loop continues as a living exercise where scarce assets, changing conditions, and the agent's prompts keep the operator deciding rather than reading a static plan.

title: Cap Table Dilution Lab
interaction: add-round composition with what-if dilution re-cascade
requirement: Expose a @rounds region with buttons to add funding events (Founders, SAFE, Seed, Series A, Series B, Option Pool), each opening inputs for amount raised, pre/post valuation, and pool %, plus a list of added rounds; an @ownership dashboard region; and a @waterfall region with a user-set exit-value input. The agent keeps an ordered ui_state stack of rounds and after each addition recomputes the fully-diluted cap table, rendering a stacked bar or pie of ownership by stakeholder across rounds, stat tiles (founder %, latest post-money, price per share), and an exit-waterfall table of payouts at the entered exit value accounting for liquidation preferences. It ui_highlights the founder wedge as it shrinks and fires ui_notify when founder ownership crosses below 50% or an option-pool top-up dilutes existing holders. The what-if loop: the user edits any prior round's terms or the exit value, and the agent re-cascades dilution through all later rounds and re-renders both the ownership dashboard and the waterfall. Concrete test: Founders 100% → SAFE $1M at an $8M cap → Seed $3M at $12M pre with a 20% pool → Series A $10M at $40M pre drops founders to ~48%, pulses the founder wedge, and toasts 'founders now minority.'

title: Rankine Cycle Composer
interaction: drag-to-compose a thermodynamic cycle the agent re-solves on a T-s diagram
requirement: Author regions: @cycle-builder (a canvas where the user drags boiler, turbine, condenser, and pump blocks into a loop and sets each block's pressure and temperature), @ts-diagram (a T-s plot), and @performance (an efficiency dashboard). The user composes a steam Rankine cycle with the boiler at 8 MPa / 500 C and the condenser at 10 kPa; each block edit updates ui_state. The agent computes the four state-point enthalpies, net work, heat input, thermal efficiency, and back-work ratio, then uses ui_render to place the state points on the ui_chart T-s diagram in @ts-diagram and ui_panel to mount stats plus a state-point table (eta ~35%) into @performance. It uses ui_highlight to mark the process with the largest exergy loss and ui_notify to warn if turbine-exit steam quality falls below 0.88 (blade erosion). Adding a reheat or regeneration block recomputes and re-renders, and the agent uses ui_ask to offer 'add a reheat stage to boost efficiency?' to drive the next iteration.

title: Tradeoff Arena
domain: weighted decision matrix with sensitivity analysis
interaction: drag criteria to reweight, agent runs flip-the-winner sensitivity
requirement: Expose @region:options (2-5 option columns), @region:criteria (draggable criterion chips reorderable by importance with a per-criterion weight nudge), @region:matrix, @region:verdict, and @region:sensitivity. The user enters options (e.g., three job offers or three vendors) and criteria; the agent builds a scored ui_panel matrix (option x criterion) with a ui_chart stacked bar of weighted contributions into @region:matrix and a ui_render verdict naming the current winner into @region:verdict. Dragging criteria to reorder or nudging a weight recomputes weighted totals, re-renders the bars, and updates the verdict, ui_notify on any winner flip. The signature feature is a sensitivity simulation in @region:sensitivity: the agent computes how much each criterion's weight would have to move to flip the winner and ui_highlight the criterion the decision is most fragile to ('Salary is doing all the work; drop its weight 15% and Offer B wins'); once a winner survives ±20% weight swings it ui_theme the accent green as a robust pick. Example: three vendors scored on price/support/security — dragging 'security' above 'price' flips the winner from A to C, and the sensitivity panel marks the decision fragile until support weight is also raised.

title: Biomarker Threshold Lab
interaction: threshold slider / ROC what-if
requirement: Regions: @distributions (overlaid diseased vs healthy score histograms with a draggable cutoff line), @roc (an ROC curve with the current operating point marked), @confusion (a 2x2 TP/FP/FN/TN table), and @metrics (stat tiles for sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, LR+, and Youden J). The user drags the cutoff or moves a slider and the page posts the threshold via ui_state; the agent recomputes every operating metric at that cutoff, redraws the confusion matrix, moves the ROC operating point, and ui_highlight pulses whichever metric the user is optimizing. A ui_ask sets the clinical context (disease prevalence and the cost ratio of false-negative vs false-positive), which shifts the agent's recommended optimal threshold (Youden vs cost-weighted) and drops a ui_notify when the user's manual cutoff diverges from the recommendation. Concrete: a troponin-like marker at cutoff 0.04 gives sensitivity 0.92 / specificity 0.78; sliding to 0.10 raises specificity to 0.94 but sensitivity falls to 0.71, and under a 10:1 FN:FP cost the agent flags the higher cutoff as unsafe and highlights the sensitivity tile. The loop is drag threshold -> recompute all metrics -> re-render panels + attention shift, with the ui_ask cost context reshaping the recommendation.

title: Protege Tutor Lab
interaction: learning-by-teaching with an AI protege whose belief meters adapt to your explanations
requirement: Cast the learner as the teacher: expose an @region:avatar showing an AI 'student' with a set of belief meters on a topic (Newton's third law), several deliberately wrong (belief 'heavier objects fall faster' at 80%), a @region:teach explanation input, and a @region:transcript. The human types explanations; the agent role-plays the confused student, updating each belief meter in ui_state based on whether the explanation actually targeted it, and asks a naive follow-up via ui_ask ('but if I drop a bowling ball and a feather...?'). Well-aimed explanations swing a misconception meter from red toward green and log a milestone in the transcript, while vague ones leave it stuck and the avatar stays confused. The agent tracks which misconceptions the teacher has and hasn't addressed in ui_state and steers its student-questions toward the untouched ones; ui_highlight pulses a meter when it flips and ui_notify fires when the student 'gets it'. Concrete drive: the teacher explains equal-and-opposite forces, so the 'action-reaction cancels out' meter turns green while 'heavier falls faster' stays red, prompting the avatar to raise the feather-vs-ball question. The avatar's overall understanding % is the win condition.

title: Stance Coalition Compass
interaction: multi-axis stance sliders mapping to a live coalition space
requirement: The page exposes an `@axes` region with 5 labeled policy sliders (economic, social, environmental, security, institutional-trust, each -10..+10), a `@map` region, and a `@coalitions` region. As the user moves any slider the page writes the 5-vector to ui_state; the agent places the user as a point in a 2D coalition space via ui_graph/scatter, computes distance to a set of named coalition archetypes (e.g., 'Eco-populist', 'Market liberal', 'Communitarian'), and renders a ui_chart (nearest-coalition affinity bars) plus a ui_table (issue -> which coalition you agree/clash with) into `@coalitions`. It uses ui_highlight to pulse the coalition you're closest to and, as you drag, ui_notifies the moment a slider move crosses a realignment boundary ('moving security +4 just flipped your nearest ally from Eco-populist to Communitarian'). It uses ui_ask to run a what-if ('Which single issue are you least willing to compromise?') and locks that axis while showing the best-fit coalition given the constraint. Example: starting centrist then dragging environmental to +9 snaps the nearest coalition to Eco-populist and highlights security as your biggest clash. The loop: move slider -> recompute coalition map -> agent redirects attention to your realignment and trade-offs.
